synthesizedFacts.fact: Sun damage, also known as photoaging, is primarily caused by ultraviolet (UV) light exposure, which can lead to premature aging and increase the risk of skin cancer.
Common signs of sun damage include wrinkles, pigmentation changes (such as sun spots and freckles), loss of skin elasticity, and broken capillaries.
Sun damage can be prevented by using sunscreen, wearing protective clothing, and avoiding peak sun exposure times.
While DNA damage from UV exposure cannot be reversed, treatments such as retinoids, chemical peels, and laser therapy can improve the appearance of sun-damaged skin.
